text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The paper quotes an unspecified finance ministry document as saying the ministry was planning to introduce tax on yields from state securities which should tax also state papers issued before the new law becomes effective.
- Slovakia's foreign trade turnover totalled 322.085 billion crowns in the fist half of 1997, an increase of 12.7 percent over the same period last year.
The Slovak finance ministry has approved an increase in the maximum allowed motor fuel prices by around 0.50 crowns per litre, effective from August 1.

- The state-owned energy monopoly Slovenske Elektrarne (SE) said reconstruction of Slovakia's only operating nuclear power plant at Jaslovske Bohunice will cost 5.5 billion crowns by the year 1999. The SE plans to spend some 1.3 billion on the plant's reconstrucion this year.

SME - U.S. ambassador to Slovakia, Ralph Johnson, on Wednesday said it was now time for the Slovak parliament to decide on the Constitutional Court ruling that the parliament last December violated Jozef Gaulieder's rights when it voted to withdraw his mandate.
- Johnson said the U.S. administration will take its official stance on Gaulieder's case after the Slovak parlaiment decides on the issue.

- The ethnic Hungarian Christian Democratic Movement (MKDH) said it supported other opposition parties in their attempt to call an extraordinary session parliamentary to demand the return of Gaulieder's mandate.

- The opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said the only way how to solve the current political crisis was a radical change in the country's leadership in the next general elections scheduled for 1998. The SDL, however, said the current ruling coalition might attempt to manipulate the elections to retain power.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Stefan Gavornik, President of the Slovak privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF) said he would welcome opposition representatives in NPF bodies in order to improve control over the privatisation process.
